## 401026bab1f6

**Classification: suspected teaching shortcut, reproduced over current source support.** No source was changed.

Candidate rival: **reflect color-4 marks only inside frames that contain at least two such marks**. This rival fits all four canonical pairs: their per-frame color-4 mark counts are `[2]`, `[3]`, `[3]`, and `[3]`. It also fit all 960 ordinary generated grids sampled across easy/medium/hard; every generated frame contained at least two marks.

The exact lawful counterexample is `checks/audit/401026bab1f6/singleton_input.json`. It contains one framed region with a single color-4 mark. The target generator’s `self_check` accepts it. The intended rule reflects that mark to color 7 at the symmetric frame position, while the rival does nothing. `checks/audit/401026bab1f6/singleton_racket_output.json` is the selected Racket result. `authority_check.json` binds generator SHA-256 `e98763349e5291f922a8edc80ab57ff4fc822babf15ad3e2d16639f9b7f23d83` and rule hash `5539aa3ad4f4`, and confirms Racket matches the independent intended output and disagrees with the rival.

Reproduction/probe: `checks/audit/401026bab1f6/probe_singleton_mark.py`; full observations: `singleton_probe.json`. This is a support/teaching gap, not evidence that the reference rule is wrong. A repair should allow singleton-mark frames in ordinary lessons and declare the minimum-two shortcut as a rival.
